text.p: The Turkish lira eased to 86,980 per dollar from 86,760 at Monday's close due to a higher dollar/mark and the central bank's dollar rate for banks' compulsory hard currency transfers set at 86,900 lira.
Bankers said financial markets were quiet after U.S. missile strikes on military targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north.
"Some customers who were worried by the recent developments were buying hard currencies, but there was no negative reaction from banks," said a private bank dealer.
They said the markets instead focused on the Treasury's 112-day bill auction which met heavy demand.

Overnight money rates traded between 65.5-74.5 percent during the day, and the central bank drained 4.4 trillion lira at 50 percent at the close. It had lent banks 17.4 trillion lira at 75 percent on Monday.

The treasury sold 133.8 trillion lira worth of December 25, 1996 paper, meeting more than half of a total 234.9 trillion lira of bids. It slashed the average yield to 117.5 percent from 135 percent at the previous 189-day t-bill auction on August 27.
A cash shortage is expected for Wednesday when banks cash in 83 trillion lira from the treasury for maturing t-bills but will pay 104 trillion lira for the auction.
The central bank said it would open a five-day repo auction on Wednesday to feed cash to the system.
T-bill yields fell by one-to-two points across the board because of heavy demand for the auction.

The yield on the most heavily traded February 26 paper fell to 130.10 percent from 131.94 at Monday's close. The second most active February 12 paper yielded 129.11 percent, down from Monday's 131.24 percent.
December 25 papers sold in today's auction also traded lower at 115.06 percent with Wednesday's value date after the auction. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
